title: Quasi-coherence of the pushed-forward increasing-tuple sheaf terms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$ separated, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ a finite family of affine opens, and $G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Each degree $i\in\mathbb Z$ of $f_*(\operatorname{extend} C(U,G))$ [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction] is quasi-coherent. Neither a covering assumption nor boundedness of $G$ beyond being a module in degree zero is required.

source.place: Tags 01FM, 02KG and 02KH; termwise sheaf and affine comparison before cohomology

proof.text: For nonnegative degree p, the existing term comparison identifies the constructed sheaf term with the finite product of open pushforwards. Every nonempty tuple intersection is affine: compose separated f with the terminal morphism of Spec A and use IsAffineOpen.iInf. Restriction preserves quasi-coherence, and pushforward from each affine intersection to Spec A is quasi-coherent by the qcqs-pushforward theorem (affine morphisms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated). The pushforward composition isomorphism transfers this property to each f_* j_t* term.

The pushed-forward product is quasi-coherent: replace each quasi-coherent factor on Spec A by tilde of its global sections via the counit, and combine these using Pi.mapIso with the finite-product preservation isomorphism for the additive tilde functor. The resulting product is isomorphic to a tilde module, hence quasi-coherent. Transfer along pushforward of the extension-degree isomorphism, pushforward of the existing term comparison, and PreservesProduct.iso. For degrees outside the embedding image, use isZero_extend_X and preservation of zero objects; compare to tilde of the zero module, which is quasi-coherent.
